audio.strategy: Phase 2 has three recorded, bundled, offline sample sets (Grand, Upright, Electric) played through per-note sample voices, plus three honestly synthesized types (Clav, Digital, Misc) and the Phase 1 live-synthesis voice as a labelled fallback. Every sound reaches one AudioContext through per-layer buses, the ordered effect units, the shared Rotary, a master gain, and a limiter. Recorded audio is never generated, and generated audio is never described as a recording.

sampleSources.name: Salamander Grand Piano V3 (Yamaha C5), bundled as public/samples/grand
sampleSources.source: Alexander Holm, Salamander Grand Piano V3, distributed by FreePats (freepats.zenvoid.org/Piano/acoustic-grand-piano.html) as SalamanderGrandPianoV3+20161209_44khz16bit.tar.xz, sha256 58750eb1366761e187f71ddb9b932355ea894d28ec4331e74ab8acb44c819936. Upstream sample rate 44.1 kHz, 16-bit WAV.
sampleSources.attribution: Salamander Grand Piano V3 by Alexander Holm, licensed CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Attribution is required when this set is redistributed.
sampleSources.rootNotes: MIDI 27 (D#1) to 99 (D#7), every third semitone from the upstream minor-third grid; 25 roots.
sampleSources.velocityLayers: 4 of the 16 upstream layers: v3 (1-47), v7 (48-79), v11 (80-106), v15 (107-127). Upstream layer ranges are replaced by these four.
sampleSources.processing: Re-encoded from WAV to MP3 (libmp3lame, 80 kbps, stereo). Each file is cut to 10 seconds with a 1.5-second fade-out, so sustain beyond about 10 seconds is silent. No loop points are used. Hammer and pedal-noise releases and the pedal-down string samples are not bundled.
sampleSources.notes: Pitch from the upstream pitch_keycenter. Nearest-root playback never shifts a note more than 1.5 semitones inside the keybed (checked by tests).

sampleSources.name: UprightPianoKW (Kawai upright), bundled as public/samples/upright
sampleSources.source: FreePats, UprightPianoKW-SFZ+FLAC-20220221.7z (freepats.zenvoid.org/Piano/acoustic-grand-piano.html#UprightKW), sha256 3a66da3b25a2fd9499d90bcf09f1aee4431825796e249361b48af59b1201e703. Recorded by Gonzalo and Roberto in January 2017 on a Zoom H1 in a living room; processed by Roberto with free software.
sampleSources.attribution: Public domain dedication (CC0 1.0). Attribution is not required; the recording credits are kept in public/samples/licenses/upright-readme.txt.
sampleSources.rootNotes: 38 roots from the upstream SFZ, MIDI 21 (A0) to 108 (C8), at the upstream pitch_keycenter.
sampleSources.velocityLayers: 2 upstream layers: vL (1-80) and vH (81-127). 28 of 38 roots have both layers; 10 roots have only the soft layer, so loud strokes at those roots use the soft layer (declared gap).
sampleSources.processing: Re-encoded from FLAC to MP3 (libmp3lame, 80 kbps, stereo), full upstream length (about 5 to 8 seconds). The upstream loop points are not used, so sustain beyond the end of a sample is silent.
sampleSources.notes: Pitch from the upstream pitch_keycenter. The shift from the nearest root is at most 2 semitones inside the keybed (checked by tests).

sampleSources.name: 1977 Rhodes Mark I Stage 73 (jRhodes3d), bundled as public/samples/electric
sampleSources.source: Jeff Learman, jRhodes3d-wav, GitHub jlearman/jRhodes3d-wav at commit a886e6cebf074c995a10634f82ebe4fdb90f5ca6, folder jRhodes3d-mono-wav, mapping _jRhodes3d-mono-no-xfade-wav.sfz. The author recorded his own 1977 Rhodes Mark I Stage 73 in about 2006, directly from the harp connector, with EQ applied by him.
sampleSources.attribution: jRhodes samples by Jeff Learman, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. Attribution is required. Non-commercial use only; commercial use needs the author's permission (contact in the LICENSE file).
sampleSources.rootNotes: 15 roots, MIDI 29 (F1) to 96 (C7), every fourth or fifth white key, at the upstream keycenter.
sampleSources.velocityLayers: 5 discrete layers from the no-crossfade mapping: 1-47, 48-72, 73-95, 96-111, 112-127. Every root has all five layers.
sampleSources.processing: Re-encoded from mono WAV to MP3 (libmp3lame, 80 kbps, mono). Each file is cut to 10 seconds with a 1.5-second fade-out. The upstream samples are unlooped, so sustain beyond about 10 seconds is silent. The stereo and crossfade variants are not bundled.
sampleSources.notes: The LICENSE file in the upstream repository says CC BY-NC 4.0 for distributing the samples. A comment in the SFZ header says CC-SA-BY 'without share-alike or attribution'. This build follows the stricter LICENSE file. The set is non-commercial. Keys 97 to 100 play from the C7 root and are shifted up to about 4 semitones; keys 28 and 29 are shifted by 1.

generatedSources.name: Phase 1 additive piano voice (live synthesis)
generatedSources.description: Six sine partials per note with a small inharmonic stretch, velocity-dependent partial levels and low-pass cutoff, and exponential decay. Generated at note-on. Used as the labelled fallback for Grand, Upright, and Electric while their sets load or after they fail. Not a recording.

generatedSources.name: Clav (synthesized)
generatedSources.description: Sawtooth plus square oscillators through a decaying low-pass filter with a short decay and quick release. An approximation of clavinet character, not a model of the Clavinet D6 pickups (manual p. 24).

generatedSources.name: Digital (synthesized FM)
generatedSources.description: Two-operator FM: a sine carrier with a sine modulator whose index decays after the strike, giving a bell-like upper spectrum. A stand-in for digital piano character.

generatedSources.name: Marimba (synthesized)
generatedSources.description: Three inharmonic sine modes at ratios 1, 4, and 10 with fast decay on the upper two.

generatedSources.name: Simulated sympathetic string resonance
generatedSources.description: When a note is struck with String Res on and other keys are held, each held note rings at its fundamental at a low level for about 3 seconds. A simulation of the effect described on manual p. 25; no pedal-down samples are used.

generatedSources.name: Generated reverb impulse responses
generatedSources.description: Six room impulse responses generated at run time from a fixed-seed noise generator with per-type decay (Booth 0.22 s to Cathedral 4.5 s), early reflections, and spring echoes for Spring. Not recordings of real rooms.

notes: Sample files live in public/samples/ and are fetched relative to the page, so the build works offline from any folder (base './'). Nothing is fetched from the network at runtime.
The sample sets were built by tools/samples/build_piano_samples.py from the three upstream archives. The script is the provenance record for every file.
Unison, Dyn Comp, KB Touch, Timbre, Soft Release, and Master Level act on the rendered signal through gains, curves, and filters; they are not separate recordings.
Organ, Synth, and Program sound engines are not in Phase 2; their panel controls are decorative and say so.

Declared gaps: Upright has 10 soft-only roots; Grand is truncated at 10 seconds; Upright plays its full length; Electric is non-commercial (CC BY-NC 4.0) and is shifted by up to about 4 semitones at its extremes; no pedal-down string samples and no pedal noise; soft and sostenuto pedals are not implemented (SUSTPED is); Clav and Misc timbre steps reuse the acoustic set as an approximation; the piano model dial is decorative because each type has one model.
